title: backlog.py cost dates a reopened item by its first done, and states the no-line cause as fact from the time alone
goal: Found in the SP-s5fdczv7 review of ST-dets7lkp: bl_cost.item_done_time takes min() over the commits git log -S finds for the done status, so an item reopened and done again is dated by its first done, and a re-done after the newest run reads unnamed or an old date; and the before-first-sidecar and after-newest-run reasons name a cause (no capture hooks yet; not distilled or delivered yet) as fact from the done time alone, though a host with capture off reads the same. item_done_time gives the time of the item's last transition to done, the two reasons say what the time shows and that the cause is the likely one, the repro exits 0, and backlog.md's Cost of work says so.

run: import os,sys,json,subprocess,tempfile;from pathlib import Path;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_cost as b;t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());g=lambda *a,**e:subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(t),*a],check=True,capture_output=True,env={**os.environ,**e});g('init','-q');g('config','user.email','a@example.com');g('config','user.name','a');f=t/b.REL_DIR/'ST-aaaaaaaa.json';f.parent.mkdir(parents=True);w=lambda s,d:(f.write_text(json.dumps({'id':'ST-aaaaaaaa','status':s},indent=2)),g('add','-A'),g('commit','-qm',s,GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=d,GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=d));w('doing','2026-01-01T00:00:00Z');w('done','2026-01-03T00:00:00Z');w('doing','2026-02-01T00:00:00Z');w('done','2026-03-01T00:00:00Z');r=b.item_done_time(t,'ST-aaaaaaaa');print('done time of a reopened item:',b.epoch_iso(r) if r else r);sys.exit(0 if r and b.epoch_iso(r).startswith('2026-03-01') else 1)

notes: Probe (2026-10-07): git log -S on the done status also matches the reopen commit that removes it (a reopened item now doing gave ['2026-02-01', '2026-01-03']), so max() over the -S times is as wrong as min(): the fix tells the commit that adds the done status from the one that removes it.
